newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Jan-March GDP up 1.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Jan-March GDP up 1.6 pct.

text.p: The following is a selection of analysts' initial reactions to Japan's January-March gross domestic product (GDP) data, which the government said on Friday rose a real 1.6 percent quarter on quarter, or an annualised 6.6 percent. For fiscal 1996/97, Japan's GDP grew 3.0 percent in real terms.
KENNETH COURTIS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE BANK GROUP ASIA:

"Bond markets are going to be looking like a train wreck later this afternoon. These are very good numbers. This is going to lead everyone to revise upward their (GDP) forecasts for the (1997) calendar year to 2.5 percent."
JANE BERRYMAN, SENIOR ANALYST, TECHNICAL DATA:

"I don't believe we will have an ODR (official discount rate) hike anytime soon just because of this very historical piece of data, greatly influenced by consumption and other factors, has come out higher than expected."
HISASHI YAMADA, ECONOMIST, JAPAN RESEARCH INSTITUTE:

"Consumption appears to have been strong and external demand also boosted growth. Of course, this was ahead of the consumption tax hike, so there will be a reaction in the next quarter. The issue is, what will be the total growth for the six months through June?
"I don't think that the decline in consumption (in the April-June quarter) will be such as to completely offset the rise in January-March, and external demand should be a plus as well."

He said the Bank of Japan was likely to want to see the data for April-June as one factor in deciding whether to raise interest rates, but that other factors such as the yen's rise would be taken into account by the central bank.
"It would be difficult to raise rates right away in September," he said.
YASUSHI OKADA, DEPUTY DIRECTOR, SECURITIES INVESTMENT ADVISORY DEPARTMENT, DAIWA SECURITIES:
"I expect both spending and capital investment to slump in the April-June quarter in reaction to the surprisingly robust spending growth of an annualised 20 percent for the January-March quarter.

"The Bank of Japan is likely to hold on to its relaxed monetary policy until they examine data for July-September. It is yet uncertain whether Japan will be able to maintain capital investment growth of around an annualised three percent for July-September as in January-March."
